From 94a8cea54cd935c54fa2fba70354757c0fc245e3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Brian Foster <bfoster@redhat.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 12:19:05 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] ext4: fix dirtyclusters double decrement on fs shutdown

fstests test generic/388 occasionally reproduces a warning in
ext4_put_super() associated with the dirty clusters count:

  WARNING: CPU: 7 PID: 76064 at fs/ext4/super.c:1324 ext4_put_super+0x48c/0x590 [ext4]

Tracing the failure shows that the warning fires due to an
s_dirtyclusters_counter value of -1. IOW, this appears to be a
spurious decrement as opposed to some sort of leak. Further tracing
of the dirty cluster count deltas and an LLM scan of the resulting
output identified the cause as a double decrement in the error path
between ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() and the caller
ext4_mb_new_blocks().

First, note that generic/388 is a shutdown vs. fsstress test and so
produces a random set of operations and shutdown injections. In the
problematic case, the shutdown triggers an error return from the
ext4_handle_dirty_metadata() call(s) made from
ext4_mb_mark_context(). The changed value is non-zero at this point,
so ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() does not exit after the error
bubbles up from ext4_mb_mark_context(). Instead, the former
decrements both cluster counters and returns the error up to
ext4_mb_new_blocks(). The latter falls into the !ar->len out path
which decrements the dirty clusters counter a second time, creating
the inconsistency.

To avoid this problem and simplify ownership of the cluster
reservation in this codepath, lift the counter reduction to a single
place in the caller. This makes it more clear that
ext4_mb_new_blocks() is responsible for acquiring cluster
reservation (via ext4_claim_free_clusters()) in the !delalloc case
as well as releasing it, regardless of whether it ends up consumed
or returned due to failure.

Fixes: 0087d9fb3f29 ("ext4: Fix s_dirty_blocks_counter if block allocation failed with nodelalloc")
Signed-off-by: Brian Foster <bfoster@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Baokun Li <libaokun1@huawei.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260113171905.118284-1-bfoster@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Theodore Ts'o <tytso@mit.edu>
Cc: stable@kernel.org

diff --git a/fs/ext4/mballoc.c b/fs/ext4/mballoc.c
index de4cacb740b3..dd29558ad753 100644
--- a/fs/ext4/mballoc.c
+++ b/fs/ext4/mballoc.c
@@ -4186,8 +4186,7 @@ ext4_mb_mark_context(handle_t *handle, struct super_block *sb, bool state,
  * Returns 0 if success or error code
  */
 static noinline_for_stack int
-ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(struct ext4_allocation_context *ac,
-				handle_t *handle, unsigned int reserv_clstrs)
+ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(struct ext4_allocation_context *ac, handle_t *handle)
 {
 	struct ext4_group_desc *gdp;
 	struct ext4_sb_info *sbi;
@@ -4242,13 +4241,6 @@ ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(struct ext4_allocation_context *ac,
 	BUG_ON(changed != ac->ac_b_ex.fe_len);
 #endif
 	percpu_counter_sub(&sbi->s_freeclusters_counter, ac->ac_b_ex.fe_len);
-	/*
-	 * Now reduce the dirty block count also. Should not go negative
-	 */
-	if (!(ac->ac_flags & EXT4_MB_DELALLOC_RESERVED))
-		/* release all the reserved blocks if non delalloc */
-		percpu_counter_sub(&sbi->s_dirtyclusters_counter,
-				   reserv_clstrs);
 
 	return err;
 }
@@ -6333,7 +6325,7 @@ ext4_fsblk_t ext4_mb_new_blocks(handle_t *handle,
 			ext4_mb_pa_put_free(ac);
 	}
 	if (likely(ac->ac_status == AC_STATUS_FOUND)) {
-		*errp = ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(ac, handle, reserv_clstrs);
+		*errp = ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(ac, handle);
 		if (*errp) {
 			ext4_discard_allocated_blocks(ac);
 			goto errout;
@@ -6364,12 +6356,9 @@ ext4_fsblk_t ext4_mb_new_blocks(handle_t *handle,
 out:
 	if (inquota && ar->len < inquota)
 		dquot_free_block(ar->inode, EXT4_C2B(sbi, inquota - ar->len));
-	if (!ar->len) {
-		if ((ar->flags & EXT4_MB_DELALLOC_RESERVED) == 0)
-			/* release all the reserved blocks if non delalloc */
-			percpu_counter_sub(&sbi->s_dirtyclusters_counter,
-						reserv_clstrs);
-	}
+	/* release any reserved blocks */
+	if (reserv_clstrs)
+		percpu_counter_sub(&sbi->s_dirtyclusters_counter, reserv_clstrs);
 
 	trace_ext4_allocate_blocks(ar, (unsigned long long)block);
 
-- 
2.34.1



diff --git a/fs/ext4/mballoc-test.c b/fs/ext4/mballoc-test.c
index a9416b20ff64..4abb40d4561c 100644
--- a/fs/ext4/mballoc-test.c
+++ b/fs/ext4/mballoc-test.c
@@ -567,7 +567,7 @@ test_mark_diskspace_used_range(struct kunit *test,
 
 	bitmap = mbt_ctx_bitmap(sb, TEST_GOAL_GROUP);
 	memset(bitmap, 0, sb->s_blocksize);
-	ret = ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(ac, NULL, 0);
+	ret = ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(ac, NULL);
 	KUNIT_ASSERT_EQ(test, ret, 0);
 
 	max = EXT4_CLUSTERS_PER_GROUP(sb);

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### Modifications per File

**1. `fs/ext4/mballoc.c`**
- **`ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()`**:
  - Removed the `reserv_clstrs` parameter and the associated code that decremented `s_dirtyclusters_counter` for non‑delalloc allocations.
- **`ext4_mb_new_blocks()`**:
  - Updated the call to `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` to omit the removed parameter.
  - Moved the decrement of `s_dirtyclusters_counter` (by `reserv_clstrs`) from the conditional block inside `out:` (which only ran when `!ar->len` and non‑delalloc) to an unconditional release at the end of the function (if `reserv_clstrs > 0`). This ensures the reserved cluster count is always released exactly once after the allocation attempt, regardless of success or failure.

**2. `fs/ext4/mballoc-test.c`**
- Adjusted the test call to `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` to match the new signature (no `reserv_clstrs` argument).

### Relationships Between Changes
- The removal of the `reserv_clstrs` parameter and the decrement logic from `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` is the core fix. It eliminates a double decrement scenario: previously, when `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` failed (e.g., due to a shutdown), it could decrement the dirty clusters counter, and then the caller `ext4_mb_new_blocks()` would decrement it again in its error/out path. By centralizing the release in the caller and performing it unconditionally (only if `reserv_clstrs` is non‑zero), the counter is decremented exactly once.
- The test change is a trivial adaptation to the updated API of `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()`, ensuring the test compiles correctly.

The patch fixes a double decrement of the `s_dirtyclusters_counter` in ext4's block allocator, which could occur during filesystem shutdown. The modifications are in two files:

## fs/ext4/mballoc.c
- Changed `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` to no longer accept a `reserv_clstrs` parameter and to remove the direct decrement of `s_dirtyclusters_counter` for non-delalloc allocations.
- Updated the call to `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` in `ext4_mb_new_blocks()` to pass only two arguments (removing `reserv_clstrs`).
- Modified the cleanup path in `ext4_mb_new_blocks()` to unconditionally decrement `s_dirtyclusters_counter` by `reserv_clstrs` (if non-zero), instead of conditionally decrementing only when `ar->len == 0` and not a delalloc reservation. ## fs/ext4/mballoc-test.c
- Updated the test call to `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` in `test_mark_diskspace_used_range()` to match the new two-argument signature (removed the third argument `0`).

**Relationship**: The main fix consolidates the dirty cluster counter decrement into `ext4_mb_new_blocks()`, preventing a double decrement that occurred when `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` failed and then the caller also decremented. The test file is updated to keep the unit test compatible with the changed function interface.

## Summary of Modifications

### 1. `fs/ext4/mballoc.c` — Core Fix

- **Removed `reserv_clstrs` parameter** from `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()`.  
  This function no longer handles the dirty clusters counter decrement.

- **Deleted the `percpu_counter_sub(&sbi->s_dirtyclusters_counter, reserv_clstrs)` call** inside `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()`.  
  This was the first decrement that could cause a double decrement when the function returned an error.

- **Updated the call site** in `ext4_mb_new_blocks()`:  
  `*errp = ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(ac, handle, reserv_clstrs);`  
  → `*errp = ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(ac, handle);`

- **Consolidated the dirty clusters release** into a single location at the end of `ext4_mb_new_blocks()` (after the `out:` label):  
  - Removed the old conditional decrement inside the `if (!ar->len)` block (which was the second decrement causing the bug).  
  - Replaced with a simple unconditional decrement:  
    `if (reserv_clstrs)`  
    `    percpu_counter_sub(&sbi->s_dirtyclusters_counter, reserv_clstrs);`  
  This ensures that regardless of whether allocation succeeded or failed, the reserved clusters are released exactly once.

### 2. `fs/ext4/mballoc-test.c` — Test Update

- **Updated the call to `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()`** in the test function to match the new signature:  
  `ret = ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(ac, NULL, 0);`  
  → `ret = ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(ac, NULL);`  
  (Removed the third argument `0`.)

---

### Relationship Between the Changes

The test file change is a direct consequence of the signature change in `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` in `mballoc.c`. Since the test calls that function, it must be updated to match the new prototype. The core logical fix is the relocation of the dirty clusters counter decrement from `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` (which could be executed in an error path) to the caller `ext4_mb_new_blocks()`, where it is performed exactly once after all outcomes. This eliminates the double decrement that occurred when an error from `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` was propagated and then `ext4_mb_new_blocks()` also decremented the counter in its error handling path.

        Root cause:
        The dirty clusters counter (s_dirtyclusters_counter) was decremented twice when an error occurred during block allocation. First in ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() for non-delalloc allocations, and then again in ext4_mb_new_blocks() in the error path (when ar->len is zero). This double decrement caused the counter to go negative, triggering a warning in ext4_put_super().
        
        Commit message:
        ext4: fix dirtyclusters double decrement on fs shutdown

fstests test generic/388 occasionally reproduces a warning in
ext4_put_super() associated with the dirty clusters count:

  WARNING: CPU: 7 PID: 76064 at fs/ext4/super.c:1324 ext4_put_super+0x48c/0x590 [ext4]

Tracing the failure shows that the warning fires due to an
s_dirtyclusters_counter value of -1. IOW, this appears to be a
spurious decrement as opposed to some sort of leak. Further tracing
of the dirty cluster count deltas and an LLM scan of the resulting
output identified the cause as a double decrement in the error path
between ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() and the caller
ext4_mb_new_blocks().

First, note that generic/388 is a shutdown vs. fsstress test and so
produces a random set of operations and shutdown injections. In the
problematic case, the shutdown triggers an error return from the
ext4_handle_dirty_metadata() call(s) made from
ext4_mb_mark_context(). The changed value is non-zero at this point,
so ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() does not exit after the error
bubbles up from ext4_mb_mark_context(). Instead, the former
decrements both cluster counters and returns the error up to
ext4_mb_new_blocks(). The latter falls into the !ar->len out path
which decrements the dirty clusters counter a second time, creating
the inconsistency.

To avoid this problem and simplify ownership of the cluster
reservation in this codepath, lift the counter reduction to a single
place in the caller. This makes it more clear that
ext4_mb_new_blocks() is responsible for acquiring cluster
reservation (via ext4_claim_free_clusters()) in the !delalloc case
as well as releasing it, regardless of whether it ends up consumed
or returned due to failure.
